operations.summary: Submits a single, self-contained question to Fin and starts a non-conversational request. Fin returns its answer asynchronously through the `fin_replied` event and completes the conversation without an `awaiting_user_reply` cycle.
operations.description: Ask Fin a single, self-contained question and receive one informational answer. Unlike a conversation, `/fin/ask` is non-conversational: Fin will not ask follow-up questions, will not run procedures, and will not escalate to a human on its own. You can still escalate one yourself with `POST /fin/escalate`; the ask conversation is already closed after its one-shot answer, and escalation leaves it closed while routing the handoff separately. Fin's answer is delivered asynchronously via the `fin_replied` event. The conversation ends with a `complete` status — there is no `awaiting_user_reply` cycle. {% admonition type="warning" %} To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**. {% /admonition %}

operations.summary: Applies an asynchronous bulk action to up to 1,000 Knowledge Hub content items. Choose an action and provide content IDs of supported types; actions can publish, unpublish, delete, change availability or audience, or update tags. The request is enqueued for background processing, and items with unsupported types for the selected action may be silently dropped.
operations.description: Asynchronously run a bulk action over up to 1,000 Knowledge Hub content items. Six actions are supported: * `publish` and `unpublish` — apply to `article_content` only. * `delete` — permanently delete content (excludes synced sources and `external_content`). * `set_availability` — toggle Fin AI Agent, Copilot, and Sales Agent availability flags. * `set_audience` — manage segment membership on content. * `update_tags` — apply and/or remove existing tags on content. Unlike the other actions, `update_tags` addresses articles by the parent `article` id, not `article_content`. Tags must already exist and not be archived; supply at least one of `add_tag_ids` / `remove_tag_ids`. The endpoint validates the request, enqueues background work, and returns 202 with a placeholder envelope. Items whose `type` is not in the action's allowlist are silently dropped before processing. Articles imported from synced sources (Confluence, Notion, Zendesk, Salesforce Knowledge, etc.) are silently skipped on `delete` — they can only be removed by disconnecting the underlying import source. Requires the `write_content` OAuth scope.

operations.summary: Creates contacts in bulk using an asynchronous job; this is a strict create operation and does not update existing contacts. Supply up to 100 contact objects in `contacts`; items that match an existing contact by `external_id` or `email` are rejected while other items can still be created. Use the returned job ID with GET /contacts/bulk/{id} to check progress and identify whether items were rejected.
operations.description: You can bulk create contacts by submitting an array of contact objects. This is a **strict create** and never updates an existing contact. The endpoint creates an async job that processes the items in the background. Use the returned job ID with `GET /contacts/bulk/{id}` to check the job status. Only the fields listed in the request schema below can be set. Any other fields in a contact object are ignored. {% admonition type="info" name="Handling existing contacts" %} If a contact already exists with the given `external_id` or `email` (including an archived contact), that item is rejected and the job's `state` ends as `completed_with_errors`. New contacts in the same request are still created. The job `state` from `GET /contacts/bulk/{id}` is the signal that one or more items were rejected. Created contacts aren't returned with IDs in the response. Look them up afterwards with Get a contact by External ID or Search contacts. {% /admonition %} {% admonition type="info" name="Limits" %} - Maximum of 100 contacts per request. - You can append tasks to an existing job by including `job.id` in the request body. - Tag application is best-effort and processed asynchronously: unknown tag IDs are skipped, and per-tag results are not returned in the job status. {% /admonition %}

operations.summary: Deletes multiple contacts permanently through an asynchronous job. Include up to 100 contact identifiers in `contacts`; an item that cannot be deleted fails independently, while the job continues processing other items. Use the returned job ID with GET /contacts/bulk/{id} to monitor the job and check for item failures.
operations.description: You can delete contacts in bulk by submitting an array of contact `id`s. The endpoint creates an async job that processes the deletes in the background. Use the returned job ID with `GET /contacts/bulk/{id}` to check the job status. {% admonition type="warning" name="Permanent deletion" %} A contact that doesn't exist, or can't be deleted, fails that item and the job's `state` ends as `completed_with_errors` (visible via `GET /contacts/bulk/{id}`) without failing the rest of the batch. {% /admonition %} {% admonition type="info" name="Limits" %} - Maximum of 100 contacts per request. - You can append tasks to an existing job by including `job.id` in the request body. {% /admonition %}

operations.summary: Updates multiple contacts in an asynchronous job by applying the supplied fields to each identified contact. Include an `id` and the fields to change in each contact object, with no more than 100 objects in `contacts`. Use the returned job ID with GET /contacts/bulk/{id} to monitor progress; tag application is best-effort.
operations.description: You can bulk update contacts by submitting an array of contact objects with the fields to update. Each contact must include an `id` field identifying the contact to update. You can also add or remove tags on each contact by including a `tags` object. Only the fields listed in the request schema below can be set. Any other fields in a contact object are ignored. The endpoint creates an async job that processes the updates in the background. Use the returned job ID with `GET /contacts/bulk/{id}` to check the job status. {% admonition type="info" name="Limits" %} - Maximum of 100 contacts per request. - You can append tasks to an existing job by including `job.id` in the request body. - Tag application is best-effort and processed asynchronously: unknown tag IDs are skipped, and per-tag results are not returned in the job status. {% /admonition %}

operations.summary: Submits an event associated with a user, lead, or visitor for tracking. Include `event_name`, `created_at`, and one contact identifier: `id`, `user_id`, or `email`; event metadata supports up to 10 flat keys. Use an access token with write permissions and send the request as JSON.
operations.description: You will need an Access Token that has write permissions to send Events. Once you have a key you can submit events via POST to the Events resource, which is located at https://api.intercom.io/events, or you can send events using one of the client libraries. When working with the HTTP API directly a client should send the event with a `Content-Type` of `application/json`. When using the JavaScript API, [adding the code to your app](http://docs.intercom.io/configuring-Intercom/tracking-user-events-in-your-app) makes the Events API available. Once added, you can submit an event using the `trackEvent` method. This will associate the event with the Lead or currently logged-in user or logged-out visitor/lead and send it to Intercom. The final parameter is a map that can be used to send optional metadata about the event. With the Ruby client you pass a hash describing the event to `Intercom::Event.create`, or call the `track_user` method directly on the current user object (e.g. `user.track_event`). **NB: For the JSON object types, please note that we do not currently support nested JSON structure.** | Type | Description | Example | | :-------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | String | The value is a JSON String | `"source":"desktop"` | | Number | The value is a JSON Number | `"load": 3.67` | | Date | The key ends with the String `_date` and the value is a [Unix timestamp](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time), assumed to be in the [UTC](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time) timezone. | `"contact_date": 1392036272` | | Link | The value is a HTTP or HTTPS URI. | `"article": "https://example.org/ab1de.html"` | | Rich Link | The value is a JSON object that contains `url` and `value` keys.…

operations.summary: Creates an asynchronous export job for message delivery and engagement data about outbound content. Provide `created_at_after` and `created_at_before` as Unix timestamps; the inclusive date range selects messages by when they were sent, not when they were updated. Only one export job can be active per workspace.
operations.description: To create your export job, you need to send a `POST` request to the export endpoint `https://api.intercom.io/export/content/data`. This endpoint exports **message delivery and engagement data** for outbound content (Emails, Posts, Custom Bots, Surveys, Tours, Series, and more). The exported data includes who received each message, when they received it, and how they engaged with it (opens, clicks, replies, completions, dismissals, unsubscribes, and bounces). It does not export raw message or conversation content. The only parameters you need to provide are the range of dates that you want exported. >🚧 Limit of one active job > > You can only have one active job per workspace. You will receive a HTTP status code of 429 with the message Exceeded rate limit of 1 pending message data export jobs if you attempt to create a second concurrent job. >❗️ Updated_at not included > > It should be noted that the timeframe only includes messages sent during the time period and not messages that were only updated during this period. For example, if a message was updated yesterday but sent two days ago, you would need to set the created_at_after date before the message was sent to include that in your retrieval job. >📘 Date ranges are inclusive > > Requesting data for 2018-06-01 until 2018-06-30 will get all data for those days including those specified - e.g. 2018-06-01 00:00:00 until 2018-06-30 23:59:99.

operations.summary: Creates a message initiated by an admin as an in-app message, email, or WhatsApp message. Choose a `message_type` and provide the fields required for that type, including a sender and recipient. Set `from.type` to `admin`; using a user or lead as the sender instead creates a contact-initiated conversation and causes `to`, `cc`, and `bcc` to be ignored.
operations.description: You can create a message that has been initiated by an admin. The conversation can be either an in-app message, an email or whatsapp. > 🚧 Sending for visitors > > There can be a short delay between when a contact is created and when a contact becomes available to be messaged through the API. A 404 Not Found error will be returned in this case. This will return the Message model that has been created. > 🚧 Retrieving Associated Conversations > > As this is a message, there will be no conversation present until the contact responds. Once they do, you will have to search for a contact's conversations with the id of the message. {% admonition type="warning" name="Messages from contacts" %} `from` should be an admin. A request with a user or lead as `from` is not rejected: it creates a conversation initiated by that contact, as the Create a conversation endpoint (`POST /conversations`) does, and the `to`, `cc` and `bcc` fields are ignored. To create a conversation initiated by a contact, use `POST /conversations`. {% /admonition %}

operations.summary: Creates or updates a tag, or applies or removes a tag from companies or users. Supply the fields for the operation you want to perform; each operation returns a tag object.
operations.description: You can use this endpoint to perform the following operations: **1. Create a new tag:** You can create a new tag by passing in the tag name as specified in "Create or Update Tag Request Payload" described below. **2. Update an existing tag:** You can update an existing tag by passing the id of the tag as specified in "Create or Update Tag Request Payload" described below. **3. Tag Companies:** You can tag single company or a list of companies. You can tag a company by passing in the tag name and the company details as specified in "Tag Company Request Payload" described below. Also, if the tag doesn't exist then a new one will be created automatically. **4. Untag Companies:** You can untag a single company or a list of companies. You can untag a company by passing in the tag id and the company details as specified in "Untag Company Request Payload" described below. **5. Tag Multiple Users:** You can tag a list of users. You can tag the users by passing in the tag name and the user details as specified in "Tag Users Request Payload" described below. Each operation will return a tag object.

operations.description: Hand a conversation off to a human teammate. If you use the Intercom Helpdesk, the handoff lands in your team inbox. Provide either `conversation_id` or `user`: - `conversation_id` — escalate an existing agent conversation, including one started with `/fin/ask`. On the Intercom Helpdesk, Fin by default summarises the conversation and opens a new Helpdesk conversation that carries the summary as an internal note. Escalation does not change the original agent conversation's assignment or open/closed state. Configure an escalation Operator Workflow to change this default. - `user` — escalate on behalf of a user with no prior agent conversation. On the Intercom Helpdesk, a new Helpdesk conversation is created for the teammate. Not supported on Fin for Platforms — see below. In both cases, pass the optional `context` to give the receiving teammate background your orchestrating agent has and Fin does not. On the Intercom Helpdesk, it appears above the summary in the internal note of the new conversation the teammate picks up. It is never shown to the end user. Escalating an existing conversation also sets its AI Agent resolution state to `escalated`, readable as `ai_agent.resolution_state` on the Conversations API. This is a resolution state, not a billable resolution. On Fin for Platforms, `conversation_id` is required — `user` is not supported and is rejected, because there is no Intercom Helpdesk in which to create a conversation. There is no Intercom inbox either, so an escalation that no workflow handles does not open a Helpdesk conversation for a teammate. `context` is not surfaced, and the conversation is left open for your platform to hand off and continue driving. You are notified over the existing webhook or SSE channel with an `escalated` status followed by `complete`. The `complete` status signals that Fin is done; it does not close the conversation. On the Intercom Helpdesk, the new human conversation remains open; on Fin for Platforms, the conversation…

parameters.name: ticket_type_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the ticket type which is given by Intercom.

operations.summary: Lists paginated status events for WhatsApp messages sent through the Outbound module. Use `ruleset_id` to select the set of messages and `per_page` and `starting_after` to paginate the results. The API plan must allow access to this operation.
operations.description: Retrieves statuses of messages sent from the Outbound module. Currently, this API only supports WhatsApp messages. This endpoint returns paginated status events for WhatsApp messages sent via the Outbound module, providing information about delivery state and related message details.

parameters.name: ruleset_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the set of messages to check status for

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of results per page (default 50, max 100)

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for pagination, used to fetch the next page of results

operations.summary: Identifies the authenticated admin and returns the associated app object, called a workspace in legacy terminology. Use this endpoint to identify the admin who is signed in. If you use it in a custom sign-in flow, do not accept sign-ins from users with unverified email addresses.
operations.description: You can view the currently authorised admin along with the embedded app object (a "workspace" in legacy terminology). > 🚧 Single Sign On > > If you are building a custom "Log in with Intercom" flow for your site, and you call the `/me` endpoint to identify the logged-in user, you should not accept any sign-ins from users with unverified email addresses as it poses a potential impersonation security risk.

operations.summary: Retrieves the execution status and result details for an asynchronous job. Use the `job_id` provided by Intercom to check whether the job is pending, successful, or failed. When the job creates a resource, the response can include its type, identifier, and URL.
operations.description: Retrieve the status of job execution.

parameters.name: job_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the job which is given by Intercom

operations.summary: Links a conversation or customer ticket to an existing tracker ticket. Supply the tracker's `ticket_id` and the `conversation_id` to link; the tracker ticket can have up to 2,500 linked conversations. This operation requires the `write_tickets` OAuth scope.
operations.description: Link a conversation to an existing tracker ticket. The conversation can be a regular conversation or one that has been converted into a customer ticket. Use this when related conversations surface after a tracker ticket has already been created. The ticket in the path must be a tracker ticket, and `conversation_id` in the body is the conversation (or customer ticket) to link to it. This returns the linked conversation. A tracker ticket can have up to 2,500 linked conversations; once that limit is reached, further requests return `linked_conversation_limit_exceeded`. Requires the `write_tickets` OAuth scope.

parameters.name: ticket_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the tracker ticket which is given by Intercom.

operations.summary: Lists the event type values available for filtering admin activity logs. Use the returned values with the `event_types` filter when searching activity logs.
operations.description: You can get a list of all activity log event types. This is useful for discovering valid values to use with the `event_types` filter on the List all activity logs endpoint.

operations.summary: Lists activity logs for admins in the app within a requested time range. Provide `created_at_after` as the start of the range and optionally use `created_at_before` to set its end. Results are paginated.
operations.description: You can get a log of activities by all admins in an app.

parameters.name: created_at_after
parameters.description: The start date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a UNIX timestamp.

parameters.name: created_at_before
parameters.description: The end date that you request data for. It must be formatted as a UNIX timestamp.

operations.summary: Lists the admins associated with the workspace. Set `display_avatar` to `true` to include each admin's avatar object and image URL; it defaults to `false` when omitted.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of admins for a given workspace.

parameters.name: display_avatar
parameters.description: If set to true, the response will include the admin's avatar object containing the image URL. Defaults to false.

operations.summary: Lists collections in the help center app. Use the results to review collection details, including their names, descriptions, and parent collections. Collections are ordered by `updated_at` in descending order, with the most recently updated first.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all collections by making a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/help_center/collections`. Collections will be returned in descending order on the `updated_at` attribute. This means if you need to iterate through results then we'll show the most recently updated collections first.

operations.summary: Lists companies, ordered by `last_request_at` and descending by default. Use the pagination parameters to retrieve results in pages; companies without associated users are excluded, and this endpoint can return at most 10,000 companies.
operations.description: You can list companies. The company list is sorted by the `last_request_at` field and by default is ordered descending, most recently requested first. Note that the API does not include companies who have no associated users in list responses. When using the Companies endpoint and the pages object to iterate through the returned companies, there is a limit of 10,000 Companies that can be returned. If you need to list or iterate on more than 10,000 Companies, please use the [Scroll API](https://developers.intercom.com/reference#iterating-over-all-companies). {% admonition type="warning" name="Pagination" %} You can use pagination to limit the number of results returned. The default is `20` results per page. See the [pagination section](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#pagination-for-list-apis) for more details on how to use the `starting_after` param. {% /admonition %}

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch. Defaults to first page

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many results to return per page. Defaults to 15

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `asc` or `desc`. Return the companies in ascending or descending order. Defaults to desc

operations.summary: Lists articles in your workspace. Results are ordered by `updated_at` in descending order, with the most recently updated articles first.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all articles by making a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/articles`. > 📘 How are the articles sorted and ordered? > > Articles will be returned in descending order on the `updated_at` attribute. This means if you need to iterate through results then we'll show the most recently updated articles first.

operations.summary: Lists an article's version history as paginated metadata, with the newest versions first. Use `locale` to filter the history to a configured locale, and use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results. Retrieve an individual version to access its full content.
operations.description: Fetch the version history of an article by making a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/articles/<article_id>/versions`. Versions are returned newest-first as a paginated list of metadata. Use `GET /articles/{article_id}/versions/{id}` to retrieve a single version with its full content. Requires the `read_articles_scope` OAuth scope.

parameters.name: article_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the article whose versions you are listing.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch. Defaults to the first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results to return per page.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Filter versions to a specific locale. Use the locale identifier (for example `en`, `fr`). If the locale is not configured for the workspace, a `400` is returned.

operations.summary: Lists the contacts associated with a specific company. Use the company identifier to retrieve its attached contacts; the response includes cursor-based pagination metadata.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all contacts that belong to a company.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the company which is given by Intercom

operations.summary: Lists audiences configured for the workspace, with pagination metadata. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results, and note that `per_page` is capped at 50.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all audiences for the workspace.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch. Defaults to first page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results to return per page. Defaults to 50. Maximum is 50.

operations.summary: Lists the away status reasons configured for the workspace, including reasons marked as deleted. Use this endpoint to retrieve reason labels and their associated identifiers, ordering, and status information.
operations.description: Returns a list of all away status reasons configured for the workspace, including deleted ones.

operations.summary: Lists all brands configured for the workspace, including the default brand. Use this operation to retrieve brand identifiers and configuration details. The default brand's ID matches the workspace ID.
operations.description: Retrieves all brands for the workspace, including the default brand. The default brand id always matches the workspace

operations.summary: Lists calls in a paginated result set. Use `page` and `per_page` to navigate the results; `per_page` defaults to 25 and has a maximum of 25.
operations.description: Retrieve a paginated list of calls.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch. Defaults to first page

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many results to display per page. Defaults to 25. Max 25.

operations.summary: Lists calls associated with the specified conversation IDs and includes transcripts when available. Supply between 1 and 20 IDs in `conversation_ids` to retrieve the matching calls. Use this endpoint when you need call details and transcript availability for a set of conversations.
operations.description: Retrieve calls by a list of conversation ids and include transcripts when available. A maximum of 20 `conversation_ids` can be provided. If none are provided or more than 20 are provided, a 400 error is returned.

operations.summary: Lists the segments associated with a specific company. Use the company identifier to retrieve the segments that belong to it.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all segments that belong to a company.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the company which is given by Intercom

operations.summary: Lists the notes associated with a specific company. Use the company identifier to retrieve its notes; the response includes cursor-based pagination metadata.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of notes that are associated to a company.

parameters.name: company_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the company which is given by Intercom

operations.summary: Lists contact activity events for the workspace, including contact creation, role updates, merges, and deletions. Results are ordered from oldest to newest. Use `starting_after` to continue from a previous page and `per_page` to control the page size, from 1 to 150.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of contact activity events for your workspace, such as when contacts are created, role updated, merged, or deleted. Events are returned oldest first. {% admonition type="warning" name="Pagination" %} You can use pagination to limit the number of results returned. The default is `50` results per page, with a maximum of `150`. See the [pagination section](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#pagination-for-list-apis) for more details on how to use the `starting_after` param. {% /admonition %}

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results to return per page. Defaults to 50, minimum 1, maximum 150.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: The cursor value from `pages.next.starting_after` in a previous response. Used to paginate through results.

operations.summary: Lists the banners that a contact currently matches so you can display them outside the Messenger. Call this endpoint when you are about to show the banners, because requesting them records an impression for each returned banner. Use each banner's `view_id` with the dismiss endpoint to record a dismissal.
operations.description: Returns the banners a contact currently matches, so you can display them on surfaces outside the Messenger (native mobile apps, kiosks, embedded tools). Each banner in the response includes a `view_id`. Use it to record a dismissal with the dismiss endpoint. A returned banner is treated as shown: requesting this endpoint records an impression for each banner returned, so call it at the point you are about to display the banners, not speculatively.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of a contact.

operations.summary: Lists the contacts merged into a given contact, with results returned in pages. Use `cursor` to continue from a previous response and `per_page` and `order` to control the results. Merge history is available only for contacts with the `user` role.
operations.description: Retrieve the paginated list of contacts that have been merged into a given contact. Only available for contacts with a `user` role. Returns a `404` if the contact is not found or has a `lead` role.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the contact to fetch merge history for.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A cursor for pagination. Pass the `next_cursor` value from a previous response to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results to return per page (default 50, max 150).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order to return results in. Defaults to descending.

operations.summary: Lists contacts in the workspace, including users and leads. Contacts merged into other contacts are excluded; only the destination contact remains in the list. Results are paginated, with 10 contacts per page by default and a maximum of 150 per page.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all contacts (ie. users or leads) in your workspace. {% admonition type="info" name="Merged contacts" %} Contacts that have been merged (via POST /contacts/merge) will not appear in list results. Only the target contact from the merge remains accessible. {% /admonition %} {% admonition type="warning" name="Pagination" %} You can use pagination to limit the number of results returned. The default is `10` results per page, with a maximum of `150`. See the [pagination section](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#pagination-for-list-apis) for more details on how to use the `starting_after` param. {% /admonition %}

parameters.name: include_merge_history
parameters.description: Pass `true` to include a `merge_history` array on each contact in the response. Only returned for contacts with a `user` role.

operations.summary: Lists the companies associated with a specific contact. Use the contact identifier to retrieve its attached companies; the response includes pagination metadata.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of companies that are associated to a contact.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom

operations.summary: Lists the segments associated with a contact. Use the `contact_id` path parameter to identify the contact whose segment associations you want to retrieve.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of segments that are associated to a contact.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom

operations.summary: Lists the subscription types associated with a contact where the contact has explicitly set a preference. Use this endpoint to retrieve both opt-in and opt-out choices; subscription types in their default state are not included.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of subscription types that are attached to a contact. These can be subscriptions that a user has 'opted-in' to or has 'opted-out' from, depending on the subscription type. This will return a list of Subscription Type objects that the contact is associated with. The data property will show a combined list of: 1.Opt-out subscription types that the user has opted-out from. 2.Opt-in subscription types that the user has opted-in to receiving. **Note:** This endpoint only returns subscriptions where the contact has explicitly configured their preference. Subscriptions that are in the default state — where the contact has not made an explicit opt-in or opt-out choice — are not included in the response.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom

operations.summary: Lists the tags attached to a contact. Use the `contact_id` path parameter to retrieve the contact's tag associations.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all tags that are attached to a specific contact.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the contact which is given by Intercom

operations.summary: Lists the content import sources configured for the workspace. Use the pagination links in the response to navigate through the source list. Each source represents an external source added to the Fin Content Library.
operations.description: You can retrieve a list of all content import sources for a workspace.

operations.summary: Lists content snippets in a workspace. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results; each page includes snippet objects and pagination metadata.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all content snippets for a workspace.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results to return per page. Max value of 50.

operations.summary: Lists conversation attributes defined for the workspace. Set `include_archived` to include archived attributes; by default, the list excludes them.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all conversation attributes for your workspace.

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description: Include archived attributes in the list. Default `false`.

operations.summary: Lists conversations and returns cursor-based pagination details with the results. Use `per_page` to set the page size and `starting_after` to continue from a cursor; the default page size is 20 and the maximum is 150. Set `include_monitors` or `include_scorecards` to include the corresponding QA results on each conversation.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all conversations. You can optionally request the result page size and the cursor to start after to fetch the result. {% admonition type="warning" name="Pagination" %} You can use pagination to limit the number of results returned. The default is `20` results per page. See the [pagination section](https://developers.intercom.com/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/rest-apis/pagination/#pagination-for-list-apis) for more details on how to use the `starting_after` param. {% /admonition %}

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many results per page

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: String used to get the next page of conversations.

parameters.name: include_monitors
parameters.description: If set to true, the response will include a `monitor_evaluations` array on each conversation with any QA monitor results that flagged it.

parameters.name: include_scorecards
parameters.description: If set to true, the response will include a `scorecards` array on each conversation with any QA scorecard results.

operations.summary: Lists instances of a custom object type, optionally filtered by an associated contact or conversation. Use `references_contact_id` or `references_conversation_id` to filter the results, or provide `external_id` to retrieve a single matching instance instead of a list. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results.
operations.description: List instances of a custom object type. Three modes are supported: - **No filter** — returns all instances for the type. - **`references_contact_id`** — returns instances associated with the given contact. - **`references_conversation_id`** — returns instances associated with the given conversation. When **`external_id`** is provided, returns a single matching instance (not a list).

parameters.name: custom_object_type_identifier
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the custom object type that defines the structure of the custom object instance.

parameters.name: references_contact_id
parameters.description: Return instances associated with the given contact ID.

parameters.name: references_conversation_id
parameters.description: Return instances associated with the given conversation ID.

parameters.name: external_id
parameters.description: Return the single instance with this external ID. When provided, the response is a single object rather than a list.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number of results to fetch.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of results per page. Maximum 150.

operations.summary: Lists workspace data attributes for contacts or companies. Use `model` to select a model and `include_archived` to include archived attributes; conversation attributes are available from `GET /conversations/attributes` instead.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all data attributes belonging to a workspace for contacts or companies. {% admonition type="warning" %} Conversation attributes are no longer returned by this endpoint. Calling without a `model` parameter no longer includes them, and `model=conversation` returns a `422` error. Use `GET /conversations/attributes` instead. {% /admonition %}

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Specify the data attribute model to return. For conversation attributes, use GET /conversations/attributes instead.

parameters.name: include_archived
parameters.description: Include archived attributes in the list. By default we return only non archived data attributes.

operations.summary: Lists paginated execution results for a specific data connector. Results cover the last hour by default; use `start_ts` and `end_ts` to change the time range and the filters to narrow the results. Request and response bodies are excluded unless you set `include_bodies` to `true`.
operations.description: Retrieve paginated execution logs for a specific data connector. Results from the last hour are returned by default. Use `start_ts` and `end_ts` to customize the time range. Request/response bodies are excluded by default. Use `include_bodies=true` to include them.

parameters.name: data_connector_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the data connector.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results per page (1-30, default 10).

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value from `pages.next.starting_after` in a previous response.

parameters.name: success
parameters.description: Filter by success status. Use `true`, `false`, or omit for all.

parameters.name: error_type
parameters.description: Filter by error type.

parameters.name: start_ts
parameters.description: Unix timestamp for start of time range (default 1 hour ago).

parameters.name: end_ts
parameters.description: Unix timestamp for end of time range (default now).

parameters.name: include_bodies
parameters.description: Include request/response bodies in the response (default false).

operations.summary: Lists the workspace's data connectors, ordered from most recently updated to least recently updated. Use `per_page` to set the page size and `starting_after` from `pages.next.starting_after` to continue through the results.
operations.description: Returns a paginated list of all data connectors for the workspace, ordered by most recently updated first. Data connectors allow workflows and AI agents to make HTTP requests to external APIs.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results to return per page. Defaults to 20, minimum 1, maximum 50.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: The cursor value from `pages.next.starting_after` in a previous response. Used to paginate through results.

operations.summary: Lists a data connector's version history, with the newest version first. Each entry is a configuration snapshot with its current status and an optional note; connectors that have never been published return an empty `data` list. Use `starting_after` to paginate, and provide one of the required version-reading OAuth scopes.
operations.description: Retrieve the version history of a data connector, newest first. Each entry is a point-in-time snapshot of the connector's configuration, with the status it has today and an optional note. Results are paginated. `pages.next` is omitted on the last page. A data connector that has never been published returns an empty `data` list. Requires the `read_data_connector_versions` or `read_write_data_connector_versions` OAuth scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the data connector.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results per page (1-50, default 20). Values outside this range are clamped, so values below 1 are treated as 1. A non-integer value falls back to the default of 20.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the value from `pages.next.starting_after` in a previous response.

operations.summary: Lists data events associated with a user or lead, identified by `user_id`, `email`, or `intercom_user_id`. Set `type` to `user` and use `summary` to request a summary response. You can list individual events only when they are less than 90 days old; summaries can include older events.
operations.description: > 🚧 > > Please note that you can only 'list' events that are less than 90 days old. Event counts and summaries will still include your events older than 90 days but you cannot 'list' these events individually if they are older than 90 days The events belonging to a customer can be listed by sending a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/events` with a user or lead identifier along with a `type` parameter. The identifier parameter can be one of `user_id`, `email` or `intercom_user_id`. The `type` parameter value must be `user`. - `https://api.intercom.io/events?type=user&user_id={user_id}` - `https://api.intercom.io/events?type=user&email={email}` - `https://api.intercom.io/events?type=user&intercom_user_id={id}` (this call can be used to list leads) The `email` parameter value should be [url encoded](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent-encoding) when sending. You can optionally define the result page size as well with the `per_page` parameter.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The value must be user

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: summary flag

operations.summary: Lists contacts in the workspace that are no longer active, including their status and identifiers that can help you locate them for recovery or deletion. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results.
operations.description: Fetch a paginated list of the contacts in your workspace that are no longer active, so you can recover ones whose `id`, `email`, or `external_id` you no longer have and then permanently delete them. Each entry carries a `status` describing why the contact is inactive: `archived`, `blocked`, `merged`, `pending_deletion`, or `permanently_deleted`. `merged_into_id` is present only when `status` is `merged`, and `external_id` and `email` are `null` for `permanently_deleted` contacts.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results per page. Defaults to `10`, with a maximum of `150`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch. Defaults to `1`.

operations.summary: Lists IDs and retained metadata for deleted conversations. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results; each page contains up to 20 results by default. Set `order` to `asc` or `desc` to control the ordering of conversation IDs.
operations.description: List all deleted conversation IDs. {% admonition type="warning" name="Pagination" %} You can use pagination to limit the number of results returned. The default is `20` results per page. You can navigate to next pages using the `page` param. {% /admonition %}

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch. Defaults to first page

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many results per page

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `asc` or `desc`. Returns the conversation IDs in ascending or descending order. Defaults to desc

operations.summary: Lists dynamic content for a workspace, ordered from most recently updated to least recently updated. Use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results; access requires the `read_dynamic_content` scope.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all dynamic content for a workspace, most recently updated first. Requires the `read_dynamic_content` scope.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: The number of results to return per page. Max value of 50.

operations.summary: Lists sender email address settings for the workspace. Use this operation to review configured sender addresses and their verification, domain, and forwarding details.
operations.description: Lists all sender email address settings for the workspace

operations.summary: Lists external pages in your workspace's Fin Content Library. Use the returned page data to review each page and its source, while the pagination object provides links and details for navigating the results.
operations.description: You can retrieve a list of all external pages for a workspace.

operations.summary: Lists the Fin capabilities available for a supplied user so an orchestrating agent can choose which action to call. Include the user's ID; if that user does not exist, Fin creates a user from the supplied details, and updates the email and attributes of an existing user.
operations.description: Return a machine-readable, per-user list of what Fin can do for a given end user, so an orchestrating agent can decide which endpoint to call. The response is audience-matched to the supplied user: each live, API-triggerable procedure is checked against that user before being included, alongside the static `reply` and `ask` actions. {% admonition type="warning" %} To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**. {% /admonition %}

operations.summary: Lists folders used to organize content. Use `parent_folder_id` to list only the direct children of a specific folder, and use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all folders for organizing content by making a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/folders`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page number

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Number of results per page

parameters.name: parent_folder_id
parameters.description: Filter folders by parent folder ID. Use this to list only direct children of a specific folder.

operations.summary: Lists the datasets and attributes available for reporting data exports. Use the returned dataset identifiers and attribute details to determine which data you can include in an export.

Lists pause and resume handling events for a conversation, including the teammate and timestamp for each event. Use this operation when you need to review when teammates paused or resumed handling. Access requires the `read_conversations` OAuth scope.
operations.description: List all pause/resume events for a conversation. These events track when teammates paused or resumed handling a conversation. Requires the `read_conversations` OAuth scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The identifier for the conversation as given by Intercom.

operations.summary: Lists URL redirects configured for a help center, ordered by most recently updated. Use the pagination parameters to browse the results; access requires the `read_help_center_redirects_scope` OAuth scope.
operations.description: You can fetch a list of all URL redirects for a help center by making a GET request to `https://api.intercom.io/help_center/help_centers/{help_center_id}/redirects`. Redirects are returned in descending order on the `updated_at` attribute. Requires the `read_help_center_redirects_scope` OAuth scope.

parameters.name: help_center_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the help center.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of results to fetch. Defaults to the first page.

operations.summary: Lists human-in-the-loop events from Fin consultations on a conversation, ordered from oldest to newest. Use the events to review consultation steps and their associated data; a consultation appears only after it has ended. Access requires the `read_conversations` OAuth scope and permission to access the conversation.
operations.description: List the human-in-the-loop (HITL) events for a conversation. When Fin is unsure of an answer it can consult a teammate before replying, proposing a draft that the teammate approves, steers with free-text feedback, or takes over. Each consultation is returned as a series of events, oldest first, across every consultation on the conversation. Requires the `read_conversations` OAuth scope, and the caller must be able to access the conversation. Events are only recorded once a consultation has ended, so a consultation still awaiting a teammate does not appear. Which fields appear in `data` depends on `event_type`: | `event_type` | `data` fields | |---|---| | `fin_consultation_started` | `channel`, `rule_threshold_percent`, `confidence_percent`, `sharp_ask`, `ask_rationale`, `issue_summary`, `customer_question` | | `fin_draft_proposed` | `draft` | | `fin_teammate_input_received` | `round_index`, `teammate_input`, `reviewer_admin_id`, `regeneration_outcome` | | `fin_draft_revised` | `round_index`, `revised_draft`, `regeneration_outcome` | | `fin_consultation_finished` | `outcome`, `approved_draft_type`, `final_draft`, `sent_text`, `reviewer_admin_id`, `duration_seconds`, `rounds_count`, `payload_truncated` | A consultation always produces a `fin_consultation_started` and a `fin_consultation_finished` event. `fin_draft_proposed` appears when Fin proposed a draft. `fin_teammate_input_received` appears once per round of teammate feedback, and `fin_draft_revised` once per round where Fin produced a revised draft in response. Notes on interpreting the response: - `hitl_cycle_id` identifies the consultation, so it is the same on every event of one consultation. It is not unique per event. A conversation can hold several consultations — a consultation that replaces an outstanding one finishes with an `outcome` of `superseded`. - `conversation_part_id` links an event to a conversation part where one exists. It is `null` in ordinary cases: teammate feedback given through the…

This means: - **GET /contacts/{id}** — Requesting the source contact by its original ID will return a `404 Not Found` error. - **POST /contacts/search** — The source contact will not appear in search results, including queries filtered by `updated_at`. - **GET /contacts** — The source contact will not appear in list results. Only the target contact (`into`) remains accessible. If your application stores contact IDs, update them to use the target contact's ID after a merge. {% /admonition %}

operations.summary: Previews a contact merge without changing any contact data. Supply the source and destination IDs in `from` and `into`, and optionally set `custom_attribute_names` to include selected custom attributes in the preview. The result reports whether the merge is allowed and provides either a summary of changes or reasons it is not allowed.
operations.description: Preview the result of merging one contact into another without applying the merge. This is a read-only dry run: it reports whether the merge is allowed and, if so, exactly what would change, **without modifying any data**. Send the same `from` and `into` contact IDs you would pass to Merge two contacts. You can merge a contact with a `role` of `lead` into a contact with a `role` of `user`. You can optionally pass `custom_attribute_names` to include specific custom attributes in the previewed attribute changes. - When `allowed` is `true`, the response contains a `summary`: every attribute change (with the resulting value on the surviving contact) and, for each object type, two counts — `from`, how many are on the source contact and would move to the destination, and `into`, how many the destination already has. Counts are reported for conversations, tickets, phone calls, notes, and tags. `conversations` counts non-ticket conversations only; tickets are reported separately under `tickets`, and `phone_calls` is present only for phone-channel merges. - When `allowed` is `false`, the response contains `reasons`. Each reason has a stable `code` you can branch on and a human-readable `message` you can display. {% admonition type="warning" name="Previewing non-duplicate contacts" %} By default a merge requires the two contacts to share an identifier (email or phone). Set `skip_duplicate_validation` to `true` to preview a merge of contacts that don't, the same rule the merge endpoint enforces. {% /admonition %} When `allowed` is `false`, `reasons[].code` is one of: | code | meaning | | --- | --- | | `source_same_as_target` | The source contact (`from`) and the destination contact (`into`) are the same contact. A contact can't be merged into itself. | | `invalid_merge_role_pair` | The `from`/`into` roles aren't mergeable. `into` must be a user. | | `no_shared_identifier` | The contacts share no email or phone. Set `skip_duplicate_validation` to preview anyway. | |…

You'll get an error message if you try to have more than one open per app. - If the scroll isn't used for 1 minute, it expires and calls with that scroll param will fail - If the end of the scroll is reached, "companies" will be empty and the scroll parameter will expire {% admonition type="info" name="Scroll Parameter" %} You can get the first page of companies by simply sending a GET request to the scroll endpoint. For subsequent requests you will need to use the scroll parameter from the response. {% /admonition %} {% admonition type="danger" name="Scroll network timeouts" %} Since scroll is often used on large datasets network errors such as timeouts can be encountered. When this occurs you will see a HTTP 500 error with the following message: "Request failed due to an internal network error. Please restart the scroll operation." If this happens, you will need to restart your scroll query: It is not possible to continue from a specific point when using scroll. {% /admonition %}

See the 'Link' header for the canonical contact." }] } ``` The `Link` header contains the path to the final merge target, resolving multi-hop merge chains (up to 3 hops). {% /admonition %}

operations.summary: Starts a Fin conversation using the user's message, user details, and any supplied conversation context. Include the conversation ID, message, and user; Fin processes the conversation asynchronously and signals completion through a webhook.
operations.description: Initialize Fin by passing it the user's message along with conversation history and user details. These additional pieces of context will be used by Fin to provide a better and more contextual answer to the user. {% admonition type="warning" %} To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**. {% /admonition %} Once Fin is initialized, it progresses through a series of statuses such as *thinking*, *replying*, *awaiting_user_reply*, or *resolved* before ending with a status of *complete*. During this workflow, the client should allow Fin to continue uninterrupted until a final *complete* status is returned via webhook, at which point control of the conversation passes back to the client.

operations.summary: Submits a customer's satisfaction rating for a conversation, with an optional free-text remark. Use the rating option provided in Fin's `csat_requested` event; submitting a remark locks the rating against further changes.
operations.description: Record a customer's satisfaction rating for a conversation, with an optional free-text remark. Fin decides *when* to ask for a rating — this reuses the CSAT settings on your Fin workflow, not this API. When Fin asks, it fires a `csat_requested` event over webhooks or SSE carrying the rating options to show the user. Present those options, then submit the user's choice here. Submitting the same rating again, with no new remark, is a no-op and stays successful, so an at-least-once client can safely retry. Submitting a *different* rating updates the stored rating while the update window is still open, and a first remark can be added to an already-rated survey. Once a remark has been recorded the rating is locked and can no longer be changed. {% admonition type="warning" %} To request access to the Fin Agent API, go to **Settings > Integrations > Fin Agent API** in your workspace and tell us about your use case. Once access is granted, **Fin Agent API** appears under **Fin AI Agent > Deploy**. {% /admonition %}

properties.description: The Translated Content of an Article. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the article.

properties.description: The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.

properties.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

properties.name: ai_copilot_availability

properties.name: ai_sales_agent_availability
properties.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

properties.name: scheduled_publish_at
properties.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.

properties.name: scheduled_unpublish_at
properties.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` if the article has never been published. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.

models.name: UpdateArticleRequest
models.description: You can Update an Article

properties.name: title
properties.description: The title of the article.For multilingual articles, this will be the title of the default language's content.

properties.name: description
properties.description: The description of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the description of the default language's content.

properties.name: body
properties.description: The content of the article in HTML. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. Mutually exclusive with `body_markdown`.

properties.name: body_markdown
properties.description: The content of the article in markdown. For multilingual articles, this will be the body of the default language's content. An alternative to `body` — you can provide content as markdown instead of HTML. Mutually exclusive with `body`.

properties.name: author_id
properties.description: The id of the author of the article. For multilingual articles, this will be the id of the author of the default language's content. Must be a teammate on the help center's workspace.

properties.name: state
properties.description: Whether the article will be `published` or will be a `draft`. Omitting this field leaves the publish state unchanged, so a draft stays a draft and an edit to a published article goes live immediately unless that article already has a pending draft or a scheduled publish time is set in the same request. The `PUT /articles/{id}/draft` endpoint ignores this field and always stages a draft. For multilingual articles, this will be the state of the default language's content.

properties.name: parent_id
properties.description: The id of the article's parent collection or section. An article without this field stands alone.

properties.name: parent_type
properties.description: The type of parent, which can either be a `collection` or `section`.

properties.name: translated_content
properties.description: The Translated Content of an Article. The keys are the locale codes and the values are the translated content of the article.

properties.name: folder_id
properties.description: The ID of the folder to place this article in, or null to remove it from its folder.

properties.name: audience_ids
properties.description: The list of audience IDs to assign to this article for Fin AI Agent targeting. Sending a top-level `audience_ids` broadcasts the same set to every locale. Sending `audience_ids: []` clears all audience memberships from every locale. For per-locale targeting, use `translated_content.<locale>.audience_ids` instead. Sending both top-level and per-locale in the same request causes top-level to win. Unknown audience IDs return a 404 error. No partial commit occurs.

properties.name: ai_chatbot_availability
properties.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Chatbot (Fin). For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

properties.name: ai_copilot_availability
properties.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Copilot. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

properties.name: ai_sales_agent_availability
properties.description: Whether the article should be available for AI Sales Agent. For multilingual articles, this sets the default language's availability.

properties.name: scheduled_publish_at
properties.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future publish of the article. When set together with `state: "published"`, the article is scheduled instead of published immediately. Setting `null` cancels a pending publish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Combining with `state: "draft"` returns 400 `parameter_invalid`. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_unpublish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.

properties.name: scheduled_unpublish_at
properties.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which to schedule a future unpublish of the article. Setting `null` cancels a pending unpublish schedule. Timestamps in the past or equal to the current time are rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` — the value must be strictly in the future. Rejected with 400 `parameter_invalid` if the article has never been published. Sending in the same request as `scheduled_publish_at` returns 400 — only one pending schedule per article. Empty string returns 400 `parameter_invalid`.
